report_name: Major Data Breach at Polish Healthcare Platform MyDr

threat_actors.name: MyDr Breach Attackers
threat_actors.description: The unidentified threat actors who claimed responsibility for the massive data breach at Poland's MyDr healthcare platform, exfiltrating 2.5 TB of data affecting up to 19 million citizens.
threat_actors.goals: The attackers' ultimate motive is not yet clear; they could be preparing to sell the data on cybercrime forums, ransom the data back to MyDr or the Polish government, or leak it publicly for political or ideological reasons.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Information Repositories
attack_patterns.description: The attackers accessed and stole 2.5 TB of data from the MyDr platform's primary database, which contained medical records, prescriptions, and personal identification details.

attack_patterns.name: Automated Exfiltration
attack_patterns.description: The threat actors exfiltrated a colossal 2.5 TB of data, which requires an automated and sustained effort.

identities.name: MyDr
identities.description: Poland's main healthcare platform which was the target of a massive data breach, resulting in the theft of 2.5 TB of data.

identities.name: Polish citizens
identities.description: The population of Poland, up to 19 million of whom were potentially affected by the MyDr data breach, exposing their personal and medical data.

identities.name: unnamed Polish politician
identities.description: A senior Polish politician whose personal and prescription data was leaked by the attackers to prove the authenticity of the breach.
